Commentary.Commentary: Time for the chase! The England openers, Zak Crawley and Dom Sibley, are out in the middle. The Sri Lanka players are out there as well. Spin straightaway? Yes, Lasith Embuldeniya will get the Lankans underway with the ball. Will be a tricky passage for the England players, before Tea. Here comes Lasith...

Sri Lanka never really had any partnership going, especially at the top. The wickets just kept coming and they were 6 down by the end of the first session. In the end, Embuldeniya and Lakmal provided them with a decent total. Now, whether it is enough or not, let's find out shortly as the England players step out to bat, in the chase...

From an England's perspective, it was an all-spinner show this time around, and that is reflective of the nature of the pitch as well. Bess and Leach took turns and kept chipping at the wickets, one by one. They snared 4 each, in alternate turns. A persistent 9th wicket stand saw Root bring himself in. He would get Embuldeniya, and Fernando followed him quickly, in the very next ball. The English skipper has shone with both bat and ball in this game.

Well, England need 164 to win now and it has taken them just under 36 overs to dismiss the Lankans. Sri Lanka would have been nowhere if not for the partnership between Lakmal and Embuldeniya. The rest of the batting just collapsed like a pack of cards.

OUT! Root cleans it up! Sri Lanka are all out for 126! Too full in length and outside off, Asitha tries to block it and does so well too. But somehow, the ball lands and then turns to disturb the stumps. A freak dismissal. Root has a big smile on his face, two wickets to his name now.

DRINKS! Well, Sri Lanka now have a lead of 163. Simon Doull (on air) reckoned earlier that anywhere around 170-180 and England will be finding it difficult to chase. Lasith Embuldeniya scored a handy 40 runs and well, has given himself some runs to defend, later on. Now, the last wicket must try to stretch themselves to as much as possible. Try to get the lead to another 17 runs to get that 180 first. Then they will have a decent chance. Let's see how it goes after the break as Asitha Fernando comes out to bat now.

OUT! Caught at first slip, finally! Root gets the breakthrough and it ends a fine useful knock by Embuldeniya. A tossed up ball outside off, landing full, Lasith reaches out for it and tries to push it with an open face of his blade. But it takes the outside edge and Bairstow makes no mistake this time. The 48-run stand has been broken and Sri Lanka lead by 163 runs.
Gets forward to a full ball and drives it to covers. Not in the gap.
Loopy full ball around off, it's defended solidly off the front foot.
Fullish around off, Embuldeniya runs down the track, takes it on the full and mishits it onto his boot. It deflects to the off side.
Short and outside off, Lakmal strikes it uppishly towards Leach at backward point. It though falls short of him. Almost!

FOUR! Lakmal surprising everyone here. Fuller in length and outside off, Lakmal dances down the track and looks to go inside-out over covers. Ends up mistiming it through a vacant mid off region and gets the boundary that he wanted though.

A huge appeal for LBW but not given. Maybe going down leg. Bess lands it full and on off and middle, Suranga strides forward in defense but misses. Gets hit on the pads. There is an appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Probably it was spinning in too much and would have gone down the leg side.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Fuller and on off, Lasith strides forward and nudges it in front of point. Takes a single. All valuable runs these.
Gets forward and bunts it down to mid on for a single. Very smart cricket this.
Safely negotiates the last ball as well by camping on the back foot to this flatter ball.
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
Loopy delivery on the stumps, Lasith pushes it on the off side.
Fuller in length and on off and middle, defended out.

DROPPED! Brilliant effort though. Floated ball around off, Embuldeniya goes for an expansive cover drive. Gets a good chunk off it, off the outside edge. It flies just wide of Jonny Bairstow at slip, who dives in that direction, gets his hands onto it, but drops it.
Flatter and on middle, Lasith gets a little across and taps it back on the pitch.
Joe Root brings himself into the attack now.
Short and around off, Lakmal goes onto the back foot, waits for it patiently and defends it out. Plenty of time for him to block that.
Shimmies down the track and pushes the fuller ball down to mid on, where Anderson dives well and keeps it out. Just the single.
Flatter delivery on middle and leg, Embuldeniya stays on the back foot and fends it out.
Goes back to cut this shorter ball but gets it off the outer half, to the man at backward point.
FOUR! Another slog sweep. Flighted around off, Lasith gets down and nails the slog sweep, uppishly over mid-wicket. Gets another boundary. The lead is now worth 156.
Very full length delivery on off and middle, smashed hard, but straight back to Bess, who stops it.
Floated, around off and middle, Suranga defends it out.
Taps it to second slip with soft hands there.
Short and outside off, Lasith works this on the off side for a single.

FOUR! The lead now goes past 150 here. Full and outside off, Lasith Embuldeniya lofts it over covers. Terrific shot. James Anderson, from mid off, gives it a chase, dives near the line but ends up parrying it into the fence.

FOUR! Lasith taking charge here. Flighted ball around off, Embuldeniya goes for the slog sweep. The fielder in the deep mid-wicket region runs to his left but puts in a very poor effort. Sticks his hand out to his left but the ball goes past and into the boundary. Poor effort to say the least.
Dances down and looks to keep the fullish ball on the off side. Misses though and gets hit on the body.
Presses forward to a full ball and pushes it softly to covers. The stand moves to 28, lead is 143.
Gets on the front foot and defends it on the leg side.
Aerial but in the gap! Handy runs. Full and flighted outside off, Lasith drives it through covers for one.
Whips a full ball across the line, finds the gap at mid-wicket for a single.
Stifled appeal for an lbw! Loopy ball around off, turning in, Lakmal fails to defend but is hit high on the pads. Turning too much!
Fuller and flatter on off, it's drilled down to mid on.

NOT OUT! Not a full-fledged effort from Embuldeniya to get back but he safely makes it back in. Jack tosses this around off, Lasith lets out a big stride to defend. The ball takes the inner half and goes wide of the man at leg slip. It goes to the backward square leg region and Embuldeniya wants two. The throw comes to the keeper's end and Buttler takes it and whips the bails off quickly. The umpires just want to have a look at that. Surely, not out, but still, just to check. The replays are in.... a lazy effort from Embuldeniya but he makes it back in there.
Well, we are having a look to see if a run-out was effected there. Not out, as Lasith makes it back in, even though he did not stretch there. Lazy, but survives here.
SIX! Up, up and away! Tossed up ball around off, Lasith Embuldeniya comes down and gives it a good whack. Sends it way over the bowler's head.
Quicker and flatter this time, on the body, Lasith camps back to play at it but misses and gets hit on the body.

FOUR! 'Catch' is the shout but Embuldeniya bisects the two fielders in the deep well. Full and around off, Lasith Embuldeniya gets down and goes for a slog sweep. Hits it aerial but bisects deep mid-wicket and wide long on well.
Comes down the track and pushes this fuller length delivery to the man at short mid-wicket.

An appeal for LBW but not given. Was outside the line of off stump. Full and around off, Lasith gets down to sweep but misses. Gets hit on the pads. There is an appeal for lbw but the umpire shakes his head. No review from Root here, sensible.
Allows the ball to spin back in from outside off and then blocks it back from the crease.
Shortish and outside off, Embuldeniya rocks back and punches it to sweeper cover for a single.
Tossed up ball on off, Lasith is back defending off his front foot.
EDGY FOUR! Loopy and full around off, Embuldeniya tries to drive this time but it spins away, takes the outside edge and sneaks through the gap between the keeper and first slip for a boundary.
Bess once again lands it full and close to off, Embuldeniya is forward in defense once more.
Full and flighted on off, Lasith is on the front foot in defense.
Shorter length delivery on the middle pole, Lakmal goes back and tucks it to short fine leg.
Good leave. Outside off, left alone.
Sensibly strides forward, keeping his adventurous instincts in check, and defends this full delivery to the off side.
On middle and leg, clipped through mid-wicket for one.

'Catch' is the shout..... safe! Risky, as it was going against the spin. Full length ball around off, it pitches and breaks away. Suranga looks to clear mid on with his lofted shot but the ball takes the outer half, goes uppishly and falls well short of the man at deep point. A single taken.
Full length delivery around off, nudged down to the man at mid off.
FOUR! Vital runs! Too full in length from Bess, it's around off and Embuldeniya plays a punchy drive through covers for a boundary. The lead moves to 122 runs.
Loopy and full on off, Lasith defends it off the front foot.
Identical to the last delivery, this time Lakmal gets forward and knocks it in the gap at cover-point for one.
Bess tosses it up and lands it fuller outside off, Lakmal drives but finds mid off.
Gets forward to a full ball and pushes it with an angled bat to point for a single.
Full delivery on middle and off, Embuldeniya defends it near his front pad.
And he finally is off nought. Comes down the wicket and pushes the slower through the air delivery down to long on. Takes one.
Embuldeniya nudges this fuller ball back to the bowler.
Skips down just a little and shyly pushes this fuller delivery down to mid on.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Tossed up on middle and leg, Lasith keeps it out on the on side, wants a run but is sent back.
Is Lasith Embuldeniya in now, to bat? Yes, it is him out there.

OUT! CAUGHT! Ramesh Mendis has to walk back now. Attempted to play a few shots on his debut. Departs for 16 in the second innings. Full and on off and middle, Mendis attempts another sweep. To the naked eye, he seems to have missed it. The ball appeared to have hit his pads and England go up in appeal, for an LBW. As the appeal is put in, Buttler takes the ball, which lobbed up, and appeals for a catch as well. Which one is it? Or is it neither? Umpire Dharmasena was unmoved, initially, to either. England take a bit of time and review it. First, the third umpire wants to see if there was bat involved there. Replays are in and.... yes there was bat involved. And Jos Buttler took it cleanly as well. Unfortunate way to get out. An under edge, which had lobbed off Mendis' boot.

Phew, review time, again! There is a team review for the catch. Let us go through the motions again. Is there bat there or not? What does Ultra Edge say? Yes, there is a spike as the ball passes the bat. And Buttler took the catch as well. Decision overturned.
Once again Lakmal stays inside the crease, allows the ball to spin back in and then defends it on the leg side.
Flatter and shorter on off, Lakmal blocks it off his back foot.
Quicker and flatter off spinner, Mendis goes back and turns it in the gap at mid-wicket for a run. Every run matters here.
Loopy and full around off, this time Lakmal is on the front foot as he pushes it to covers for a run.
Advances down the track to keep it out but misses and takes it on his pads.

Appeal for an lbw! Not given. Flatter delivery, around off and breaking into the batsman, Lakmal stays back to work it around but misses. He is pinged on the pads, they appeal but Bess shakes his head. Going down leg.
Slower in the air and around the off pole channel, Ramesh comes forward and fends it out.

NOT OUT! Nope, cold water poured on the English team's hopes of another wicket. It came off the top part of Mendis' arm. Even the LBW look was not out, as it was missing the wickets. Leach gives it air and bowls it on off and middle. Ramesh gets down on one knee to sweep again. The ball seemed to have taken the top part of his bat, to the naked eye's look and lobbed in front of Joe Root at second slip. He came forward and took that. There was a fervent appeal for the catch but it is not given. And right away, the skipper flashes the 'T'. There was no bat there, on the side-replay view. The LBW is examined as well and the ball is spinning away, outside the off stump line, and missing the wickets by a big margin.
Straightaway, England have taken a review! It is for a catch against Ramesh Mendis. The English players looked jubilant. Let's see if it stays that way...

FOUR! The lead moves to 113. Four welcome runs to Mendis and the Lankans. An element of risk is there when playing a shot like that though. Flighted, around the off stump line, Ramesh Mendis gets down and nails a hard sweep through backward square leg for a boundary.
Jack drops it short, outside the off stump. Lakmal rocks back and bunts it down to wide mid on. Takes a single.
Comes forward, keeps his head down, and defends this fuller delivery well.
Shortish and outside off, Suranga unconvincingly pushes it to the man at cover.
Bess drops it slightly short around off, Lakmal moves back and drags his pull shot to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Not getting forward. Lakmal sticks on the back foot to a fuller delivery and keeps it out.
Flatter off spinner on off, Lakmal defends it from the crease to point.
Suranga Lakmal is in next.

OUT! Yet another sharp catch by Zak Crawley. He is exceptionally sharp at short leg. A floated full ball landing on middle, an off spinner, Perera leans forward and flicks it across the line. He fails to keep it down and Crawley is waiting like a hawk. Completes a superb reflex catch. Mind you, it's never easy to catch those but Zak made that look very easy. Sri Lanka are effectively 107/7!
Allows the ball to spin back in from outside off and defends it from the back foot to short mid-wicket.
Advances down the track to a full ball and drives it back to the bowler. The Lankan batsman still looks to be in a rush.
Dom Bess to continue from the opposite end as well.
Short and outside the off pole line, Ramesh gets onto the back foot to cut. But he finds the fielder at point there.
On a flatter trajectory on the pads, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.

'Catch' is the call.... eventually it falls safe. Not perfectly timed shot it was. Flighted ball, outside the off pole, Perera dances down and goes aerial, inside-out, over covers. The fielder there backpedals but the ball ends up going over him and stops well short of the boundary. Two runs taken as he fields it off.
Presses forward and pushes the fuller delivery to covers.
This time Jack flights it on middle, Dilruwan looks to play it back on the track but ends up dabbing it to the man at 45, off the inner half.
Looped up, outside off, defended to the off side.
We are back after Lunch and Ramesh Mendis and Dilruwan Perera are out in the middle. The English players have taken their positions on the field and Jack Leach will continue for them.
... Day 4, Session 2...

Those dropped catches won't bother the English team much though. They know that they are very much in the game and that it is about maintaining the same discipline that they have shown throughout, so far. Sri Lanka are effectively 104/6 and 240-250 that skipper Dinesh was expecting, seems too far-fetched now. Let's see though, how they recalibrate their plans and go about, after Lunch. Join us shortly for the second session at 1240 local (0710 GMT)...

Jack Leach started the procession by removing Kusal first. Then, as if it were an almost perfectly coordinated and orchestrated play, Leach and Bess took turns to remove the Lankan batters, one by one. Mathews, Thirimanne, Dickwella - all those who played crucial knocks in the first innings - were sent packing. Dinesh fell to a loose shot, probably more in response to Joe Root's banter. Dilruwan Perera was lucky to survive a drop, alongside Mendis. Both were dropped by Root.

Earlier, at the start of Day 4, Sri Lanka cleaned up the last English wicket quickly and gained a lead of 37 runs. Stepping out to bat, to build on the same, they played the initial overs well, when seam was in play. But, England, quickly sensing that seam was not working, turned to spin. And this time, the pair of Bess and Leach delivered, and how! From 19/0, Lanka have slumped to 67/6. Could have been 7 but they can thank their stars that it wasn't.

A pulsating session comes to an end. England will feel a little that they could have had one more, but overall, it was a superlative performance from their bowlers. Or to be more specific, their spinners, who had nothing to show in the first session, but have come out all guns blazing in the second.

DROPPED! Root puts it down. England could have got 7 just before Lunch there. Maybe Joe Root is exhausted after his marathon knock earlier. Dom loops this around off, Perera comes forward and looks to block but ends up generating an outside edge there. It goes to the left of Joe Root, at slip. The English skipper goes down low in that direction, gets his left hand on it but ends up spilling it. The ball goes behind and Sri Lanka take a single. WITH THAT, IT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 4!
Dances down just a little and keeps the flighted one out on the leg side.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Lands a fuller one on the middle pole, Perera is able to fend it out on the front foot.
Flighed ball, around the off pole, Dilruwan defends it to the off side.
Dilruwan Perera makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! GONE! It is Niroshan. He has hit it aerial to covers. For the second time, in this match, Dickwella is out, on the off side. Joe is a very happy man alright. He put down Mendis earlier but looks like England will go into Lunch, with 6 wickets having been snared. Flighted delivery around off, Niroshan steps out and goes for an uppish cover drive. Dan Lawrence, at covers, takes a good catch, diving forward. It is a shot that Dickwella would never want to look at, again.
Innovative shot. The reverse sweep comes out and the batsman helps himself to a single by placing it at point.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Turning away from the batsman, Mendis slices his attempted shot towards point for a run.

DROPPED AND FOUR! Put down by Root. A cracking delivery, pitches on leg stump and turns away towards off, Mendis tries to defend but it takes the outside edge, goes low to Root at first slip who fails to catch it and the ball runs behind for a boundary. Maybe, he was late to react, thinking that Bairstow at second slip will go for it. A chance goes down begging. The lead crosses 100.
Slightly short and outside off, Ramesh goes back and cuts it to backward point
Tossed up ball landing full on off, Mendis drives it off his front foot to extra cover.
Spinning into middle and leg on a flatter trajectory, Ramesh dabs it down to mid off and pinches in a quick run.
Shortish and on middle and leg, Niroshan backs away and taps it through the covers. Takes one.

FOUR! Reverse sweep from Niroshan Dickwella. That is why there was a man in the deep but he could not catch up. Tossed up, on middle and off, ND gets down and reverses it firmly. The man at deep point runs to his right, dives, but fails to keep it out.
On off and middle, tucked to the man at deep mid-wicket and they cross.
Shorter and outside the off pole, RM rocks back and drives but finds Jimmy Anderson at mid off.
Tossed up, outside off, Ramesh Mendis lets out a stride forward and nudges it to the man at short mid-wicket.

Goodness me, that has gone over the stumps. Turn and bounce again for Leach. It lands around off and breaks back in, beating the attempted sweep shot from Dickwella. It bounces over the stumps, beats the keeper and they collect two byes.
Plays it with the spin and taps it down towards short leg.
Time for the DRS! It's for a catch at short leg. Has it gone off the inside edge? Nothing from the umpire. Joe Root is having a word with Zak Crawley and has taken the referral.

NOT OUT! A nicely tossed up ball, landing full around off, Dickwella dances down the track and tries to flick. He fails to middle his shot and it goes off his pads to the left of short leg. Crawley runs and takes the catch with a dive. They appeal. Is there any inside edge? Nopes, as far as Kumar Dharmasena is concerned. Root has a word with Crawley and takes the DRS. The Ultra Edge shows flat line and England lose a review. As a protocol, the third umpire also checked for the lbw but it's easily missing the stumps. Get on with the game...
Presses forward to a full ball and defends it to the off side.
Full and flighted on middle, Dickwella sweeps but finds short fine leg.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Short length delivery, outside the off stump channel, cut straight to Jack Leach at backward point.
Outside off, pushed to the right of Bess, who gets there and stops. Mimes a throw back to the stumps at the keeper's end. By the looks of it though, it seemed more aimed at the batter.

Goes for the sweep, but goodness me, he misses. And that one has gone just past the off stump. This time, Dom bowls a very full length off spinner, outside the off stump line, Mendis lets out a big stride forward and across, and goes for an expansive sweep. He though misses and the ball turns in, misses the off pole by just, as Jos takes it.
On middle, clipped to short leg.
Gets forward, back and then to the leg side and looks to cut the shorter length ball outside the off stump. Misses.

FOUR! Sweeps and sweeps powerfully. Off the pair and a nice way to do it. Also, a good way to get your first runs in Test cricket. Tossed up ball around the off pole line, Ramesh gets down and absolutely smokes it through square leg.
Who will walk out to bat now? The debutant, Ramesh Mendis, strides out to the middle. Got a duck in the first innings. Can he get going this time though?

OUT! Poor, poor shot selection! Have to say, Chandimal has thrown his wicket away. Calculated risk is fine but this one is just an ugly swipe across the line. Leach once again tempts the batsman with a flighted delivery, lands it full on middle, DC accepts the proposal to play another slog sweep but this time the ball spins to catch the top edge. It flies behind mid on and James Anderson turns back, takes a 360-degree turn in fact, twists and turns and does exceedingly well to pouch that skier. Brilliant, the old man has terrific hands and he has taken a stunning catch. Sri Lanka are effectively 84/5! Interestingly, before this wicket, Root chirped from first slip - 'Come on, Chandi! Throw your wicket away...' Chandimal has obliged, if we can say that!
FOUR! Excellent shot! There was an element of risk there but it paid off. Tossed up ball landing full around off, Chandimal slog sweeps it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Fuller and on off, Dickwella jumps down the track and knocks it down towards mid on for a run.
Turning away from the batsman, Chandimal follows it with the spin and taps it down to backward point for a brisk run. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses.
FOUR! Easy pickings, that! Leach drags his length short and serves it outside off, Chandimal rocks back and slaps it through covers for a precious boundary.
Ho! Ho! Ho! How to play that? Full and flighted, landing around off, Chandimal gets forward to defend but it spins away sharply to beat the outside edge. Unplayable.
A couple of dot balls to the new batsman to finish. Tossed up delivery on middle and off, Dickwella presses onto the front foot and fends it out.
Looped up on off, Niroshan comes forward and defends it out.

Niroshan Dickwella, comes out now, praying to the gods, looking up. Some chat out there, with Jonny Bairstow, probably letting out some words, in a healthy mood though. Niroshan himself is a character, he chirps a lot.

OUT! BOWLED! Sri Lanka in trouble. They have lost their fourth wicket. Spin did not do anything for the tourists in the first innings. Look at it now - 2 apiece for Leach and Bess. This time, Bess lands the off break outside the off pole line. Angelo lets out a big stride forward and across and looks to sweep. He though misses as the ball lands on the rough, comes back in sharply, and shatters the off stump.
Looped up on off and middle, defended.
Shortish length ball, around the off pole, AM dabs it safely to short leg this time.
Lands a shortish length off spinner, around off, Angelo Mathews goes back and clips it safely to the man at backward square leg.
Loopy full ball around off, Chandimal presses forward and defends it to the off side. End of a successful over.
Dinesh Chandimal walks in next.

OUT! That's a very smart and sharp catch by Zak Crawley at short leg. Leach once again gives his delivery a good toss and lands it fuller around off, Thirimanne walks forward with the flick shot but his bat turns in his hands as the ball spins to make contact. Crawley keeps his eyes on the ball and snaps a superb reflex catch. Root is ecstatic. Sri Lanka lead by 74 runs.
Gets forward and across to a full ball before flicking it to mid-wicket.
Leach looks for more flight but ends up serving a full toss outside off, Thirimanne drives it through the line but finds mid off. Misses out on a freebie.
Too full in length around off, Mathews doesn't overcommit himself forward and just pushes it in the gap at covers for a single.
Full and flighted on middle, Thirimanne moves back and helps it past short leg for a single.
Sharp turn there. Dom Bess drops a short off break, outside the off stump line, it pitches and comes back in sharply. Angelo Mathews looks to play at that but gets an inside edge onto the pads there.
Stays on the back foot and cuts the shorter length delivery through point. Gets off strike.
Flatter and outside the off stump line, Thirimanne camps on the back foot and nudges it to the off side.

Good. Good from Dan there. Got to keep the batsman on strike, to keep pressure. Fullish length ball outside the off stump line, Thirimanne strokes it to the covers region, where Lawrence dives and makes a good stop.
Looped up ball around the off stump, Lahiru is ever solid in his defence.
Shortish length ball, turning in, around the off pole line. Mathews goes back, uses the turn to work it through mid-wicket. Crosses for a run.

DRINKS! Sri Lanka in a bit of bother here, with spin coming to haunt them now. They lead by 70 runs and have 8 wickets in hand. It is a tricky phase of 1 hour now that they have to safely get through while keeping the scoreboard ticking as well. The hosts can count on the experience of Angelo Mathews and Lahiru Thirimanne to do that. The duo needs to bring all their experience into play here. Can they continue on successfully, or will the visitors clinch another breakthrough, or two? Let's find out after the mini-break...
Leach switches to over the wicket and delivers a flighted ball outside off, spinning back in, Thirimanne defends it off his back foot.
Fullish and on middle, Mathews uses his wrists and works it near the square leg umpire for a single. The bowler won't mind that shot, played against the spin.
Leach continues to be fuller and this time he is straighter as well, Thirimanne tucks it in front of square leg for a run.
Very full again, close to off, Lahiru defends it compactly off his front foot.
Flighted and very full outside off, Thirimanne defends it by getting forward.
Short and around off, turning away, Mathews reaches out for it and hits it to sweeper cover for a run.
A long discussion. Joe Root is having a word with Jack Leach. There is a deep mid-wicket put after this discussion.

Sri Lankans need to be smart and should survive, while scoring runs as well. Looped up ball around the off pole, Mathews dances down the track and flicks this down to mid on and gets off the mark, by crossing for a run. He will keep strike.
Looped up delivery outside off, Angelo sweeps straight away, getting outside the line. It hits Zak as he looked to get away from the shot. Hits his shins and falls back in the short leg region.
Who's in now? The centurion for Lanka from the first innings, Angelo Mathews, comes out to bat now. He needs to contribute here, again!

OUT! CAUGHT! Big inside edge. Double failure for Fernando. So, spin from both ends working for the English team. Bess' persistence finally pays off. He lands a loopy one on off and middle, Oshada Fernando strides forward and looks to defend that. But the ball turns when you defend like that. Turns, gets the inside edge and clips the pads. Goes to the man at short leg who takes a simple catch. Zak Crawley it is. The finger is up immediately as well. Sri Lanka are effectively 66/2!
Shortish length delivery around off, Oshada goes back and taps it to the man at leg slip, safely.
Loopy and on middle and off, Thirimanne lunges forward and pushes it through mid-wicket. Crosses for a run.
Presses forward and keeps his eyes in line with the ball. Blocks it out on the off side.
Yet another watchful defensive shot off the front foot by Oshada to complete the over.
Better this time! Full and floated close to off, Oshada this time doesn't try anything fancy, just prods forward and defends it near his front pad.

Play and a miss! Leach offers width outside off, Fernando tries to force it through the off side but it spins away to beat his bat. Needs to be careful, not the kind of pitch where you can just hit through the line.
Loopy and full outside off, an easy leave this time for Oshada.
Fuller and on off, driven off the front foot to covers. Played it with the spin.
That is defended solidly off the front foot. It's called a no ball for overstepping.
Uppish! Done in the flight. Flighted and full ball on middle, turning in, Thirimanne inside edges his attempted flick shot through backward square leg for a run.
Not a maiden, unfortunately. Fullish length delivery on the middle pole, Thirimanne lunges forward and nudges it in front of square on the leg side. Crosses for one to keep strike.
Much better over from Dom this. 5 dot balls so far. Reverts back to a fuller length, on the off pole line, Lahiru comes forward in defense there.
DB bowls another shorter one, on the off pole, LT camps back and taps it on the off side.
Now, Lahiru Thirimanne gets onto the back foot and defends this flatter one out.
Strides forward and pushes this fuller delivery to the point region.
Loopy ball outside off, left alone. Perfect. That is where Dom Bess should be.
Tossed up ball landing around off, Fernando presses forward with an angled bat and plays it close to his pads. Ends up pushing it towards point.
Again the length is a bit on the shorter side around off, Fernando punches it from the back foot to cover-point, eyes a run but is sent back.
A touch short and on off, Oshada immediately gets back in defense.
Better length. Leach drops it full and around off, drawing the batsman forward, Fernando defends it with soft hands.
Turning into the left-hander from middle, Thirimanne moves back and nudges it to fine leg for a run.
Leach drags his length short first up, it's outside off and cracked off the back foot by Oshada to deep cover. A single is taken.
Flatter ball, turning in, on middle and leg, clipped to backward square leg, for a single. Bess just struggling a bit with his length at the moment.
Drops it a bit short, outside off, Lahiru Thirimanne rocks back and strokes it through cover-point. Crosses for one.
Bowls it on the pads with the turn, worked through square leg and the batsmen cross. Oshada is off the mark!
That is not what Dom should be doing. He bowls a flatter delivery, outside the off pole, luckily for him, Thirimanne just slaps it through cover-point and gets to the other end for a single.
Goes wide of the crease and looks to drift it into the batter, it is just outside off though and Thirimanne lets it be.
Loopy delivery, outside the off pole, Lahiru comes forward but ends up leaving it.
Unplayable! Turn and bounce for Leach. It lands full and around off, Oshada gets forward to defend but it turns past the edge of his bat. Top over by Leach.
Beauty! Full and flighted around off, turning away, Oshada pushes inside the line and misses.
Tossed up ball outside off, left alone.
A touch short and outside off, Fernando stays on the back foot and cuts it late towards backward point.
Oshada Fernando is the new batsman.
DRS time! Huge shout for an lbw, the finger had gone up. Kusal Perera has a word with his partner and then takes the referral. Looks out to the naked eye, let's find out.

OUT! It's umpire's call! The decision stays as it is and it's a big breakthrough for England as Kusal Perera has a reputation to score quickly. Now we know why Leach started from 'round the wicket. He wanted to bowl as straight as possible on this surface. Does just that and bags his first wicket of the match. A flighted delivery landing full on middle, Perera goes down with the sweep shot but it goes under his bat, beats the front pad and strikes him on the stomach, right in front of the wickets. They appeal and the finger goes up. Kusal goes for the DRS after consulting his partner. The Ultra Edge finds no wood and the Ball Tracker shows it to be clipping the top of the stumps. Perera is gone! Sri Lanka are effectively 56/1.
Tossed up ball landing on middle and spinning down, Perera helps it off his pads, past leg slip for a couple of runs.
Spin from both ends! Jack Leach, it is to partner Bess from the other end. A slip, leg slip and short leg in place. Starting, strangely, from 'round the wicket.
Much better from Dom Bess. DB floats this on off, Thirimanne comes forward and blocks it.
Floated ball, outside the off pole zone, Lahiru lets it go.

That is the problem for Dom. Cannot allow the batsmen to take runs here. He floats this around the off stump zone, Perera strides forward and pushes it through the covers. Gets to the other end. He needs to keep the batsmen pinged on the crease and not allow any rotation of strike.
Hit uppishly but safe there. Shorter and around the off stump area, Kusal goes back and hits it uppishly in front of square on the off side. But it lands safely there.
Floated delivery on the off stump area, blocked.

Through him! Thirimanne possibly playing with the wrong line. Bess lands it full and around the off pole channel, Lahiru strides forward and plays it, thinking it will turn away. But it does not and skids in, goes past the inside edge of Thirimanne's bat. The keeper misses to collect and they take a bye here.
Better late than never,  they say, and the English have decided to get going with spin now. Dom Bess to bowl with the 'newish' ball now.
Around off on a length, Perera checks his drive and keeps it out towards mid off.

FOUR! And again! Perera is warming up now. Curran overpitches on this occasion, around off, Perera leans into the drive and creams it through the gap between mid of and extra cover for a boundary. The lead crosses 50.

FOUR! Fantastic shot. Curran lands it on a length around off, shaping away a bit, Perera accounts for the movement, doesn't move his front foot much and just crunches it off his back foot through covers. Lovely flow of the bat!
Pitches it on a length around middle and off, Perera sticks back and punches it down to mid off.
Curran tries to be too adventurous. Probably looking to bowl an outswinger from the middle-leg line. He ends up slipping it down the leg side, Kusal tries flicking but misses.
Slants in a length ball close to off, just a hint of away movement, Perera stays back and defends it to covers.

They look for two and will get it. Jimmy just getting a little bit too straight there. LT flicks it through square leg. The man at fine leg runs towards the ball and fields it. Two runs in the meanwhile.
Shortish length ball, angling in, on the body, dabbed to the square leg region, for a run.
Similar length but a bit closer to the off stump channel, still safe to be left alone, and Kusal Perera does just that.
Length and outside the off pole channel, Perera fends it out on the off side.

Shortish length delivery angled on the body, Perera takes a hand off and plays it with probably the gloves or the shoulder of his bat, to the square leg region. Steps out, looking for one, but is sent back.
Length ball around the off stump line, Kusal comes forward and stabs it to the man at short mid-wicket. Says 'no' to his partner for a single.
A length delivery around off, angling in, Perera punches it off his back foot past the extra cover fielder for a quick run.
Curran pulls his length back slightly on this occasion, it's outside off and Kusal attempts for the cut shot. Ends up chopping it on the off side, without much timing.
A near yorker on off, almost landing on the popping crease, Perera digs it out from the outer half of his bat to point where the fielder dives to stop the ball.
This time Curran gets closer to the middle stump line, attempting to move it away from there, Perera does well to cover the line and defends it to the on side.
Identical to the last delivery and same treatment given by the batsman. There is a hint of shape in the air for Sam but nothing much from the surface.
Starts with a full delivery around off, angling in, Perera covers the line and pushes it towards mid off.
Sam Curran to begin the proceedings from the opposite end. So, England are not thinking about spin straightaway.

3 runs from the first over. And Sri Lanka lead by 40 runs here. Fuller in length ball, outside the off stump line, Thirimanne pushes it to point, off the outer half. There is some bounce there and the ball evades Bess. Goes past him and SL get a couple. JA though is not happy with that.
Fuller in length delivery, outside the off stump, Thirimanne drives but finds cover there.
Full length ball on middle and off, angling away, Thirimanne stays back in defense and keeps it out from the outer half of his blade, towards point.

And Sri Lanka are underway. Full length ball around the off pole, Kusal Perera pushes it back to the bowler. It crashes into the ankle of the bowler and deflects to the mid-wicket region. They take a single. James Anderson is good to continue though.
That was very close to the off pole. Anderson runs in and bowls a length delivery very close to off, Perera though, judges it well, and lets it be.
Good length delivery outside the off pole, Kusal lets it be.
